tools.Name: 2d-character-sketch (yenceesanjeev)
tools.Price: Free on GitHub, MIT (github.com, checked 2026-11-13)
tools.Safety reason: a review bot code read @46ef64e: safe with the fixes in Safe install. No package.json, so no npm packages and no install hooks; the renderer draws SVG in code and runs only rsvg-convert, ffmpeg, ffprobe, git, rhubarb, macOS say and the openvoice Python, each through spawn with an argument list and no shell (scripts/sketch.mjs:55-71). Network: only the paid voices: api.elevenlabs.io (sketch.mjs:444,549,1367) and api.sarvam.ai (sketch.mjs:558); a paid send stops unless --max-chars covers it (sketch.mjs:516) and sounds/music unless --max-credits covers it (sketch.mjs:1358-1365). No telemetry. Verified behaviour and fixes: (1) API keys are read from the environment, then .env.local, .env in the working folder, then ~/.2d-character-sketch/keys.env (sketch.mjs:396-412); a key file inside a git repo that git does not ignore is refused (sketch.mjs:405-407); fix: use the free voices, or put a low-limit ElevenLabs/Sarvam key only in a gitignored .env.local. (2) install-rhubarb.sh downloads Rhubarb 1.14.0 from the official GitHub release and checks size, but the Linux build has no SHA-256 recorded (scripts/install-rhubarb.sh:17,34) and the script exits on Windows (line 18); fix: download the release zip yourself and compare its SHA-256 with the digest on the GitHub release page before unzipping. (3) install-openvoice.sh (optional, about 2 GB) pins MeloTTS to commit 2091453 and torch 2.8.0 (lines 13,23,27) but upgrades boto3/botocore unpinned (line 29), resolves MeloTTS's own requirements at install time (line 28) and downloads NLTK data and the voice model (lines 37,40); the tool calls the venv's venv/bin/python (sketch.mjs:525), a Linux/macOS path, so on Windows openvoice works only inside WSL; fix: skip openvoice, or install it only in WSL. (4) It writes into the working folder and ~/.2d-character-sketch only, and deletes only its own temp/scratch files (sketch.mjs:526,567,571,1203-1220). No fix needed beyond these.
tools.Safe install: Safe install (fixes applied): Claude Code on Windows: run it inside WSL Ubuntu (its tool paths and install scripts are Linux/macOS only). In WSL: sudo apt install librsvg2-bin ffmpeg (the commands the tool itself prints, sketch.mjs:48-51) plus Node 20 or newer; git clone https://github.com/yenceesanjeev/2d-character-sketch ~/.claude/skills/2d-character-sketch && git -C ~/.claude/skills/2d-character-sketch checkout 46ef64e. Use the free voices (no keys). Lip sync: download Rhubarb-Lip-Sync-1.14.0-Linux.zip from https://github.com/DanielSWolf/rhubarb-lip-sync/releases, check its SHA-256 against the release page, unzip it into ~/.2d-character-sketch/rhubarb and set RHUBARB to the rhubarb file inside, instead of running install-rhubarb.sh. Skip install-openvoice.sh unless you want the 2 GB local voice. Paid voices only with a low-limit key in a gitignored .env.local, and only with --max-chars / --max-credits after reading the printed estimate. claude.ai: no (needs local Node, FFmpeg and rsvg-convert). Hermes: no. Android: no.
tools.YOLO install: YOLO (your own risk): skips the commit pin, the manual Rhubarb checksum and the WSL-only openvoice rule. Copy the skill folder into %USERPROFILE%\.claude\\skills\\ (or ~/.claude/skills), then let Claude run bash scripts/install-rhubarb.sh and bash scripts/install-openvoice.sh when it asks (SKILL.md:35,149).

It writes its config to %USERPROFILE%\.bubblewrap\\config.json (packages/cli/src/lib/config.ts:28-30) and runs the JDK's keytool and the project's gradlew.bat as child processes (packages/core/src/lib/GradleWrapper.ts:42, jdk/KeyTool.ts:77). Verified behaviour and fixes: (1) on first run init offers to download JDK 17 from Adoptium on GitHub and the Android command-line tools from dl.google.com into .bubblewrap\\jdk and .bubblewrap\\android_sdk, with no checksum check (packages/cli/src/lib/JdkInstaller.ts:22-25,104-117; AndroidSdkToolsInstaller.ts:23-26,60-64), and on Windows it picks the 32-bit JDK (JdkInstaller.ts:30); fix: answer No to both prompts (config.ts:38,61) and give the paths of a 64-bit Temurin 17 JDK and the Android command-line tools you downloaded from adoptium.net and developer.android.com and checked against the SHA-256 shown there. (2) The generated Android project's Gradle wrapper downloads Gradle 8.11.1 from services.gradle.org with no distributionSha256Sum (packages/core/template_project/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties); fix: add distributionSha256Sum with the checksum from gradle.org/release-checksums before the first build. (3) build reads the keystore passwords from BUBBLEWRAP_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD and BUBBLEWRAP_KEY_PASSWORD if both are set, else prompts (packages/cli/src/lib/cmds/build.ts:78-91); fix: type them at the prompt, don't set them in the environment, keep the keystore out of git and back it up yourself. (4) validate sends the site URL to Google's PageSpeed Insights API (packages/validator/src/lib/psi/PageSpeedInsights.ts:20); only use it on a public URL. The play command uses a Google Play service-account key (packages/core/src/lib/GooglePlay.ts:232); fix: skip it and upload in Play Console by hand. Dependencies use ^ ranges; fix: exact pin and npm ci.

tools.GitHub repo: https://github.com/thuann-vn/claude-3d-animated-shorts @ f5b4c4a (MIT; HEAD on 2026-11-13; fork-style rework of mromidev/claude-animated-shorts, MIT)

tools.Safety reason: a review bot (code read @f5b4c4a, 2026-11-13, no-intake review): Safe. One skill (SKILL.md, 80 lines of instructions, no hooks, MCP server or commands) plus a local three.js engine (engine/*.js, about 1,550 lines) and small Python/Node helpers. render.cjs serves the engine folder on a random localhost port with a path check, drives headless Chrome through puppeteer-core and pipes frames to ffmpeg (lines 8-21). Network use: fetch-assets.sh downloads fixed asset files from three.js r170, Google Fonts (unpinned main branch), rsms/inter v3.19 and the Poly Haven API (lines 8-27); tools/tts.mjs sends your script text to ElevenLabs with your key (lines 6-12). main.js line 683 posts viewer OK/fix notes to a same-origin /api/feedback path that the bundled servers do not have, so nothing leaves your machine. No telemetry, no shell-outs beyond ffmpeg. Caveats: the look copies a named YouTube channel's style (style only, no frames included), so keep your own characters and stories; importmap names ez-tree and three.quarks that package.json does not install.
tools.Safe install:

This folder installs it for your user in every project; clone into the project's `.claude/skills/` instead to keep it to one project. Set CHROME to your chrome.exe path (render.cjs:6 only checks Mac and Linux paths). Voice is optional: ELEVENLABS_API_KEY in an environment variable, and set LANG_CODE and VOICE, because tools/tts.mjs defaults to Vietnamese and the author's voice id.

Network use: yt-dlp downloads the URL you give without cookies (media.py lines 48-62); _download_model fetches a whisper.cpp model from huggingface.co/ggerganov (cli.py 442-452, transcript.py 27); opt-in --transcriber elevenlabs uploads audio to api.elevenlabs.io (transcript.py 20, 201-226), with the key from the environment or a .env file in the working folder (common.py 44-56). eyes setup --fix runs installers itself: winget install Gyan.FFmpeg on Windows, brew on macOS, sudo -n apt-get on Linux (cli.py 455-470). install-skill only copies SKILL.md into ~/.claude/skills/eyes and/or ~/.agents/skills/eyes (cli.py 527-548). view and report write local HTML with no external scripts. Why caution: skills/eyes/SKILL.md section 0 and AGENTS.md tell the agent to install from unpinned git HEAD and run setup --fix 'without asking the user for routine steps', which clashes with the ask-before-install rule. Not reviewed: docs images and the explainer video. Fix-mode re-check 2026-11-15 (SKILL.md:19-30 and AGENTS.md:3,7-13 at a540961): the only risk is the shipped instruction to install unpinned HEAD and run setup --fix without asking; the fix (install it yourself pinned to a540961, delete SKILL.md section 0, never run setup --fix) covers it, so safe with fixes.
tools.Safe install:

Make sure it's installed" (SKILL.md:19-30): line 21 tells the agent to install "without asking the user", line 24 installs unpinned git HEAD and line 25 runs `eyes setup --fix`. 5) Don't run `eyes setup --fix` (it runs winget installs, cli.py:455-470); install whisper.cpp yourself and let `eyes setup` fetch the model from huggingface.co/ggerganov (cli.py:442-452). No network code at runtime: the Rust core (sudachi/Cargo.toml dependencies) and the bindings (python/Cargo.toml: pyo3, scopeguard, thread_local) have no HTTP or socket crate, and python/py_src has no urllib, requests, socket or subprocess use; the dictionary is found by importing the installed sudachidict_core package (python/py_src/sudachipy/__init__.py:44-55). jaconv is pure string conversion that imports only unicodedata, warnings and re (jaconv/jaconv.py:4-8, conv_table.py:4). Verified behaviour and fixes: (1) a Sudachi config file can name plugins by library path, and any plugin name that is not a bundled com.worksap.nlp.sudachi.* plugin is loaded as a native library (sudachi/src/plugin/loader.rs:127-141, 170); fix: use the default config (Dictionary() with no config_path) or a config you wrote, never a downloaded sudachi.json. (2) The sudachidict_core sdist's setup.py downloads the dictionary zip from a CloudFront URL with no hash check when pip builds from source (setup.py:30-51); fix: install wheels only with hashes (--only-binary=\:all\: --require-hashes), so setup.py never runs. Licenses: SudachiPy and the dictionary Apache-2.0, jaconv MIT.

No network calls, no child processes, no telemetry and no install hooks: package.json scripts have no preinstall/install/postinstall (prepack runs only when the authors publish); npm publish uses provenance (package.json publishConfig).; src/plugins/dev.ts:160-170,255-259). (2) The generated service worker caches the built site in the visitor's browser; with the default registerType 'prompt' (src/options.ts:50) the new version loads only after the user accepts the update prompt, with 'autoUpdate' it reloads on its own; fix: keep 'prompt' or show the reload toast, and use selfDestroying: true (src/modules.ts:55-71) to remove a broken worker and clear its caches. No fix needed beyond these; Node 20.19+ required (package.json engines).
